queries.query: Is there a tarot card showing a crowned conqueror riding a cube-shaped chariot under a star-covered canopy on four pillars, holding a sceptre topped by a globe, square, and triangle, drawn by one white and one black sphinx yoked together?
queries.note: Paraphrases the Chariot card's own description (coronet, cuirass, Urim/Thummim crescents, winged globe, lingam) into a simpler visual summary, keeping only unavoidable card-specific nouns.

queries.query: Does one tarot card depict a young man suspended upside-down by one foot from a gallows resting on two pruned trees, his hands bound behind him, arms folded into a downward-pointing triangle beneath his head, legs crossed to form a cross?
queries.note: Paraphrases the Hanged Man's own description; kept the gallows/inverted-hanging image since it's the card's defining visual and hard to describe otherwise, but dropped the Hebrew-letter and zodiac-sign apparatus around it.

queries.query: In this book's reading of the tarot's Devil card, is a serpent biting its own tail explained as the classic image for an inescapable, circling fate that bounds how freely a person's will can act within a fixed span of time?
queries.note: First draft ('does this book explain...') was too diffuse and missed top-15 on work survival. Strengthened by naming the Devil card directly (the card's own title, not lifted body phrasing) while still paraphrasing the ouroboros/Fatality passage itself.

queries.query: Does this book argue that the tarot is really the lost Egyptian Book of Thoth, preserved by gypsy fortune-tellers as a deck of playing cards, where each of the 22 major cards is tied to one of the twenty-two Hebrew letters as well as to a number and a symbol?
queries.note: First draft avoided the title 'Book of Thoth' entirely and missed top-15 on work survival. Strengthened by naming it directly (the book's own central thesis and title, not lifted body phrasing) and adding the gypsy-transmission detail as a second anchor.

queries.query: How do different esoteric systems argue that numbers themselves carry fixed cosmic or moral meaning, independent of what shape or object they're attached to, so that the number of a thing reveals a deeper structural truth about it?
queries.note: The book's Wronski-derived claim that the numerical order of the cards is the 'most settled element' giving 'unvarying results' — a numerology theme other traditions' own number-mysticism should also surface for.

queries.query: How do various traditions map a set of higher symbolic or divine figures onto the planets, and a set of lesser figures onto the zodiac signs and their subdivisions, so that the whole heavens become a key to reading fate or meaning below?
queries.note: The major-arcana-as-planets / minor-arcana-as-zodiac-signs-and-decans correspondence scheme as an instance of astrological-correspondence thinking other traditions' own astrology should also answer.
